system.name: Earth+
system.one_liner: an on-board satellite imagery compression system that shares fresh reference images across a satellite constellation to shrink downlink usage

content.subject: how picking reference images only from a satellite's own history versus from the whole constellation changes reference age and the fraction of tiles that must be downloaded

elements.role: receiver that downlinks the changed-tile delta for each day's image

relations.what: the delta between the current image and its chosen reference determines the changed-tile percentage
each day's captured image (or its delta) is downlinked to the ground station

panels.label: (a) three-satellite constellation
panels.differs: sets up the scenario: three satellites in different colours orbit and photograph the same area; not itself a reference-selection strategy

panels.label: (b) satellite-local reference
panels.differs: each satellite may only reference its own past images, so by Day 31/41/51 the reference is up to 30 days old, leaving 55%/65%/45% of tiles changed

panels.label: (c) constellation-wide reference
panels.differs: each satellite may reference the freshest image from any satellite via cross-coloured dashed arrows, so the reference is at most 10 days old, leaving 35%/20%/0%/45%/0% of tiles changed

values.what: the per-day percentage of changed tiles to re-download under each strategy (55/65/45% vs 35/20/0/45/0%) and the underlying reference ages (30 vs 10 days)
values.linked_by: dashed arrows colour-matched to the source satellite, connecting a chosen reference image to the day it is compared against, positioned along the shared Day 1-51 timeline
values.result_cells: boxed '% change' labels under each compared day, summarized by the orange 'many' vs blue 'much fewer' caption bars

content.key_idea: Letting a satellite pick its freshest reference image from anywhere in the constellation, not just its own history, cuts the average reference age from 30 to 10 days and the re-downloaded tile fraction from about 55% to 15%.
content.reading_order: panel (a) first for context, then left to right along the shared Day 1-51 timeline in (b) and (c), following the dashed arrows from each chosen reference image down to the ground station's % change boxes

evidence: Figure 6 gives an illustrative example of this contrast with a constellation of three satellites
the freshest reference is only ten days old rather than 30 days
reduces the age of reference images by 3× (30 days to 10 days)

summary: Figure 6 illustrates why Earth+ shares reference images across an entire satellite constellation instead of restricting each satellite to its own history. Panel (a) sets up three satellites, shown in different colours, that repeatedly photograph the same ground area while orbiting Earth. Panels (b) and (c) lay out the same Day 1-51 timeline twice: under satellite-local referencing (b), each satellite can only compare a new image against its own past images, so by Day 31/41/51 the reference is up to 30 days old and 55%/65%/45% of tiles have changed and must be downloaded; under constellation-wide referencing (c), dashed arrows instead pull the freshest available image from any of the three satellites, cutting the maximum reference age to 10 days and the changed-tile fraction to 35%/20%/0%/45%/0%. The colour-coded caption bars ('many' in orange versus 'much fewer' in blue) summarize the resulting fresher references and far smaller re-download volume.
summary_zh: 该图展示Earth+跨星座共享参考图像的机制：(a)三颗卫星拍摄同一区域；(b)仅用本星历史图像做参考，最长30天导致变化区域达55%-65%；(c)可用星座内任意卫星最新图像做参考，最长仅10天，变化区域降至0%-45%，需下载量大减。
